name: get-metric-events
description: Metric event keys LaunchDarkly has observed. Without eventKey: list recently observed event keys (query, environmentKey, dataSourceKey, limit up to 50). With dataSourceKey and eventKey: check whether that warehouse data source has produced the event. ready false means it has not been seen yet; contextKinds are the analysis units a metric on the event can use.

dataSourceKey.description: Warehouse metric data source key. Required with eventKey.

environmentKey.description: Listing only: keep events seen in this environment. Not with eventKey; a data source already belongs to one environment.

eventKey.description: Check this event key on dataSourceKey. Takes only projectKey and dataSourceKey alongside it.

limit.description: Listing only. Defaults to 50. Not with eventKey.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

query.description: Listing only: fuzzy match on event key. Not with eventKey.

name: get-contexts
description: Read LaunchDarkly contexts, the context kinds a project defines, and the attributes contexts carry. `resource` picks what to read and defaults to `contexts`. resource=kinds: the project's context kinds (e.g. `user`, `organization`, `device`) with when each was last seen. No environmentKey needed. Use it to learn which kinds exist before targeting or choosing an experiment's randomization unit. resource=attributes (environmentKey required): without `attribute`, the attribute names recently seen on contexts, optionally for one `kind`, each with a `weight` estimating how many recent contexts carry it. With `attribute` (a name from that list, such as `/country`) and `kind`, the values recently seen for that attribute, each with a weight. `prefix` narrows names or values to those starting with it. Use this to find which attribute holds a concept ("plan", "region") and which values it takes before writing a targeting clause. resource=contexts (environmentKey required): without `key`, search stored contexts by kind, key, or attribute value; returns context records with their stored attributes and when each was last seen. With `kind` and `key`, every stored instance of that one context, with its full attribute set and which SDK or application reported each instance. Search filter syntax (`filter`, resource=contexts) uses `field operator value` clauses. Operators: `equals`, `notEquals`, `anyOf`, `startsWith`, `exists`, `before`, `after`; `contains` and `notContains` are not supported. Combine clauses with `,` (AND) or `|` (OR); group with `()`. Supported fields: `kind`, `key`, `kindKey`, `name`, `applicationId`, `q` (fuzzy), and `<kind>.<attribute>` for context attributes. `kind` is emitted as the clause `kind equals "<kind>"`. Examples: - `Merchant.merchantCountryCode equals "US"` — Merchant contexts whose attribute matches - `key startsWith "merchant-"` — contexts whose key has a prefix - `applicationId equals "GoSDK/1.2"` — contexts reported by a specific SDK/application The contexts API cannot filter by which flag a context evaluated; there is no `flagEvaluated` field. Ordering is fixed by the API; there is no sort parameter. Pagination (resource=contexts): responses include `totalCount` and `continuationToken`. Pass `continuationToken` from the previous response to get the next page.

attribute.description: resource=attributes only: an attribute name such as /country; returns its values.

environmentKey.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

key.description: resource=contexts only: return every stored instance of the context with this kind and key.

kind.description: Context kind. contexts: filter, and required with key. attributes: limits names to one kind; required with attribute.

prefix.description: resource=attributes only: names, or values with attribute, starting with this text.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: save-and-start-experiment-iteration
description: Stop the current running iteration, create a new draft iteration with the provided field updates applied, and start it — the API-recommended way to mutate treatments, metrics, methodology, or other fields that are locked while an iteration is running. Provide `changeJustification` to record why a new iteration is needed. Field inputs are the same as `update-experiment`; updates are checked against the new iteration's not_started mutability rules. Fields not allowed in not_started are returned under `skipped` rather than being sent.
